questions.stem: Sheets of metal cost \(\$119.52\) each (size \(3\text{ m} \times 2\text{ m}\)), with a \(12.5\%\) discount applied. Each face of the toolbox (2 squares of \(1.8\text{ m}\times1.8\text{ m}\), 4 rectangles of \(1.8\text{ m}\times1.4\text{ m}\)) must be cut from a SINGLE sheet, though multiple faces may share one sheet if they fit without overlap. Find the minimum total cost of the sheets needed.
questions.hint: Work out how many of each face fit on one 3 m × 2 m sheet, then find the minimum number of sheets needed for all 6 faces.

steps.explain: Check how many \(1.8\text{ m}\times1.8\text{ m}\) SQUARE faces fit on one \(3\text{ m}\times2\text{ m}\) sheet: since \(1.8+1.8=3.6\) is bigger than both 3 m and 2 m, only ONE square fits per sheet — so the 2 square faces need 2 separate sheets.

Check how many \(1.8\text{ m}\times1.4\text{ m}\) RECTANGLE faces fit on one sheet: orient the 1.8 m side along the sheet\u2019s 2 m side (fits, 0.2 m spare), and along the 3 m side fit \(2 \times 1.4=2.8\text{ m}\) (2 rectangles, 0.2 m spare) — so 2 rectangles fit per sheet, meaning the 4 rectangular faces need 2 sheets.
The leftover space on a "square sheet" (a 1.2 m-wide strip) is too narrow to fit a 1.8 m or 1.4 m rectangle, so the squares and rectangles can\u2019t share sheets. Total sheets needed: \(2+2=4\).

Apply the 12.5% discount to each sheet\u2019s price, then multiply by 4 sheets.
